main_body: A wooden treasure chest overflowing with a heap of gold coins and gems, with a small loose gold pile at the lower right. The chest body is the largest volume.
top_band: Gold coin heap with a red gem, a cyan gem and a purple gem, rows ~1-8, lightest yellow/cream tones; it reads as a horizontal heaped surface seen from above
evidence: Reading the middle column from the top: purple gem tip, then the gold heap with gems and cream highlights (rows ~1-8). A lighter gold front-edge row follows at rows ~7-8, then the darker chest rim. Below that is the wooden front face with dark iron bands and a recessed keyhole lock plate (rows ~9-15). The top surface is clearly visible and several rows tall, and the front face is distinct, so it is not a front elevation. The only mismatch is that this is a chest with a heap rather than pure scattered debris, but the loose coin pile at the right fits the kind loosely.

style.evidence: The gold has about 4-5 steps (cream highlight, yellow, ochre, dark brown), and the wood has about 4 (light, mid, dark, deep) with plank grain and dark iron bands. Outlines are dark brown, tinted to the adjacent material, not neutral black. The coins carry per-coin highlights and the gems have facets. There are no large flat fills. The tiles carry many colours, comparable to the reference stall and well. It is small, but it does not look thinner or stickier than the references.
